hints.S49_A1: He RAN INTO THE BURNING BUILDING TO SAVE THE CHILD, and he is compared to a LION. Ask: does a lion stand for courage or for fear? 'Timid' and 'fearful' say he was afraid, which the sentence flatly contradicts.
hints.S49_A2: The ALARM WENT OFF, so the crew must dress fast - the GEAR has to go onto their bodies before they reach the FIRE TRUCK. Ask: which phrasal verb means to get dressed in something? 'Took off' removes it again.
hints.S49_A3: The SIREN is WAILING LOUDLY and the engine is racing to an emergency. Ask: which past verb means moved very fast? 'Crept' and 'tiptoed' are slow and quiet, and nothing FLOATS along a street.
hints.S49_A4: The people are TRAPPED INSIDE THE DAMAGED BUILDING, and he works QUICKLY AND CAREFULLY. Ask: which verb means to bring someone out of danger to safety? 'Forget', 'ignore' and 'delay' would leave them exactly where they are.
hints.S49_A5: PREVENTION is weighed against RESPONDING TO A FIRE AFTER IT STARTS - the question is which one works better. Ask: which word means producing the result you want? 'Exciting' and 'tiring' measure feelings, not success.
hints.S49_B1: The subject is EVERYONE, not 'the group' standing beside it. Words like everyone and nobody act like ONE person. Ask: which past form of 'to be' matches a singular subject? SAW tells you the time is past.
hints.S49_B2: HAS needs a past participle after it, and TWICE BEFORE ties those visits to now. Ask: what is the past participle of 'go' - the plain form, the -s form, the -ing form, or something irregular? 'Has went' is never English.
hints.S49_B3: The truck is ranked against THE WHOLE FLEET, not against one other vehicle, and it can EXTEND TO THIRTY METRES. Ask: for a short adjective, which ending marks the very top? And does a comparative ever follow 'the' like this?
hints.S49_B4: The FIRE CAPTAIN GAVE THE ORDER at one sudden moment, and the crew had already begun the job. Ask: which choice keeps an action running in the past until something cuts across it? Two options sit in the present, so they are out at once.
hints.S49_B5: SMOKE cannot be counted, and THEY HAD CAUGHT IT EARLY tells you the amount was small. Ask: which word partners an uncountable noun? 'A few', 'many' and 'several' all need things you can count one by one.
hints.S49_B6: The statement is negative - the EQUIPMENT was not CHECKED THIS MONTH. Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag flip to positive? The tag must echo the same helping verb, so 'is' and 'isn't' cannot appear here.
hints.S49_B7: A LEAFLET cannot post itself TO EVERY HOUSEHOLD - the fire service did that LAST MONTH. Ask: which choice puts the receiver in the subject position and sets the action in the past? Two options make the leaflet the doer.
hints.S49_B8: The officer is passing on a rule about CANDLES left UNATTENDED. Ask: after 'told + person', does English use a plain verb, an -ing form, or 'to' + verb? And does the negative word come before that little word, or after it?
hints.S49_C1: A FIRE ENGINE cannot wash itself - the crew does that AFTER EACH CALL-OUT, every single time. Ask: which box phrase makes one singular engine the receiver, in the present? Two box phrases talk about people being trained.
hints.S49_C2: ALL FIREFIGHTERS is a plural subject, and the training lasts AT LEAST TWO YEARS before they may attend a real fire. Ask: which box phrase uses a plural present helping verb, with the firefighters receiving the action, not doing it?
hints.S49_C3: The date 1987 fixes the time in the past, and THIS FIRE STATION is one single building that could not build itself. Ask: which box phrase is singular, past and passive? A plural helping verb would clash with one station.
hints.S49_C4: THREE PEOPLE is plural, BY THE CREW names the doer, and LAST TUESDAY EVENING fixes the time. Ask: which box phrase is plural, past and passive? The people trapped in the flat did not save themselves.
hints.S49_C5: THE FIRE SAFETY MANUAL is one single book, and SINCE IT WAS FIRST PUBLISHED runs from the past right up to now. Ask: which box phrase is a singular present perfect passive? A plural helping verb would not agree with one manual.
hints.S49_C6: NEW SMOKE DETECTORS is plural, and SINCE LAST YEAR again stretches from the past up to now. Ask: which box phrase is a plural present perfect passive? The detectors certainly did not put themselves up.
hints.S49_C7: RIGHT NOW tells you the work has not finished - it goes on as we speak. Ask: which box phrase shows a passive action in progress at this very moment? A simple present passive would mean it happens as a routine.
hints.S49_C8: THE ALARM SOUNDED at one sudden moment, and work on the LADDER TRUCK had already begun. Ask: which box phrase shows a passive action still in progress in the PAST when something interrupted it? A finished past passive hides the interruption.
hints.S49_D1: The blank names the FIREFIGHTERS themselves - the people who do the job. Ask: which box word is a noun meaning the staff of an organisation? 'Apparatus' names their equipment, not the men and women who carry it.
hints.S49_D2: The blank follows TO, so it must be a plain verb, and the fire is only pretend - it happens SAFELY inside a TRAINING ROOM. Ask: which box word means to copy a real situation for practice?
hints.S49_D3: The dash defines it: ANYTHING THAT COULD START OR SPREAD A FIRE. Ask: which box word names a source of danger? A 'casualty' is a person who gets hurt - that is the result, not the cause.
hints.S49_D4: The clue is USING STAIRWAYS INSTEAD OF LIFTS - everyone is getting out fast. Ask: which box word means to leave a building because of danger? 'Extinguish' is what you do to the flames, not to the building.
hints.S49_D5: The examples come after SUCH AS: BREATHING EQUIPMENT and HYDRAULIC CUTTING TOOLS. Ask: which box word is the general noun for specialist gear? 'Personnel' would name people, but the blank names things.
hints.S49_E1: THE FIREFIGHTERS is plural - a whole crew standing there in FULL GEAR. Ask: which past form of 'to be' agrees with a plural subject? Find the subject first, then make the verb match it.
hints.S49_E2: Stretch the underlined word into two words: 'IT IS ESSENTIAL to check your smoke alarm'. Does that work? Then an apostrophe is missing. Without one, the word means 'belonging to it', and nothing here owns the checking.
hints.S49_E3: No C stands in front of the underlined word, so the plain rule holds: I before E. Ask: which two letters has the writer swapped in 'PEICE'? The same order shows up in shield, thief and relief.
hints.S49_E4: SPREAD is the verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW the fire travels - fast. Ask: which word class describes an action, the adjective or the adverb? An adjective would need a noun to describe, and there is none here.
hints.S49_E5: The breathing masks belong to the RESCUERS - a whole team of them. Ask: when the owners are plural and the word already ends in -s, where does the apostrophe sit? One owner would place it differently.
hints.S49_F1: Put the SMOKE ALARM fact first: it is the thing that has to be done. Ask: after UNLESS, does the verb stay in the present? And does that clause still need a 'not' inside it, when UNLESS already means 'if not'?
hints.S49_F2: Both facts have the same doer, so the FIREFIGHTER is named only once. Ask: which action came earlier, and can that earlier verb be turned into an -ing form straight after AFTER? A comma then joins the two halves.
